output:
Here's a draft you can forward as-is. I've left one spot for your sister's number so people have a way to reach you directly — drop it in where marked and delete the note.

---

# Open letter from Thandi — please pass this on

*(If you're reading this because someone forwarded it to you: I'm Thandi, a kindergarten teacher at Little Acorns Pre-Primary in Mowbray. My flat burned down in a fire at Lindale Court on Station Road, Observatory, on Saturday night. I'm safe. I'm writing this letter because my phone has not stopped since Saturday morning and I honestly cannot keep up with replying to everyone one by one — I have read every single message and cried at more of them than I'd like to admit. Please don't be hurt if I don't reply straight away, and please feel free to forward this to anyone you think should read it.)*

## I'm OK

I'm safe. That's the first thing and the most important thing. I'm staying at my sister's in Rondebosch and I've had a bed, a desk to work at, and a freezer full of food I didn't even have to ask for. My family is fine. I'm tired, and my head is a bit foggy from the smoke, but I'm okay.

I know a lot of you have been worried, and I don't want anyone sitting on that worry any longer than they have to. So here is everything, in one place, as plainly as I can say it.

## What happened (the short version)

The fire started at around 11:40pm on Saturday 7 November, in a ground-floor flat at Lindale Court — not mine. I'm on the second floor, flat 12. The fire department has told us it was probably an electrical fault, but they're still investigating, and I'm not going to guess at anything until they have it properly confirmed. I'd rather tell you nothing than tell you something wrong.

Everyone got out. All fourteen flats were emptied. Two people were treated for smoke at Groote Schuur and sent home the same night. Nobody was hurt, and I don't say that lightly — I know how close it was.

My flat took the worst of the smoke and the water. The ceiling came down in the lounge. My landlord says nobody goes back in for at least six weeks.

## How I got out

Uncle Faizel, our neighbour, went door to door on our floor in his vest and slippers, banging and shouting. That's how I woke up. I am so grateful to that man. I grabbed my phone and my cat, Marmalade, and nothing else — no bag, no documents, nothing. Marmalade hid under the car for two hours afterwards, which I only found out about on Sunday morning, and I cried with relief. Furniture can be replaced. Marmalade can't.

I lost a lot of things. Some of them are just things. But there's one I'd like a little help with: I had taken home all the laminated stuff for the end-of-year concert — 22 crowns for the Ladybirds and the children's handprint banner we made together. That banner is gone. I'd like to make it again if I can.

## The fundraiser — this is the real one

My friend Zinhle set up a BackaBuddy page for me. Zinhle, I love you, and I hate asking for help, but you told me to shut up and accept it, so I'm accepting it.

**backabuddy.example/thandi-lindale-court**
Target: R25 000. It was at R11 400 this morning.

If you want to help, please use that page. Zinhle is handling it and keeping track of everything.

## ⚠️ Please watch out for the fake one

Since Saturday there are **two other things going around claiming to help me, and they are not mine.**

- A page called **"Thandi Fire Relief"** on another fundraising site.
- A WhatsApp message asking people to **EFT money to a Capitec account.**

Neither of those is me, and neither of those money requests goes to me. I have reported both. If somebody sent you one of those links or account details, please don't pay it, and please send it on to whoever messaged you so we can stop it. I've already had people very kindly telling me they'd paid into it, which makes me feel sick, so please spread the word — the only legitimate page is the BackaBuddy link above.

## What I actually need

I'm being specific, because vague requests don't help anyone.

1. **Help with the deposit for a new place.** This is the big one. Once I have a deposit and a key, I can start putting my life back in order. If you know of a flat, a rental agency, or a landlord who could move quickly, or if the BackaBuddy page can cover the deposit for me, I would be so grateful.
2. **A laptop.** If anyone has an old one that still works, please consider it for me. Every single lesson plan I've written for five years was on my laptop, and it's gone. I need to be able to plan and print for the Ladybirds by Wednesday.
3. **School shoes and work clothes, size 6 / size 34.** That's the only clothing I need.

## What I do NOT need

- **Clothes in general.** I have far too many already, thank you. If you were thinking of donating clothes, please give them to the other flats at Lindale Court — their families lost everything too, and they'd get more use out of them than I would.
- **Food.** My sister's freezer is full. Genuinely. If you want to help, the deposit or the laptop would be worth a hundred times more than a food parcel.

That bag of clothes one of the mums left on the gate at my sister's at 7am on Sunday without knocking — I found it, and I'm wearing some of it right now. Thank you. Please don't do it like that though, it makes me feel like a charity case. Just ask me first, or ask Zinhle, and I'll tell you what I need. I'd rather be honest with people than be handed things I can't use.

## For the school families

A few things for the mums and dads:

- **The concert on 27 November is still happening.** The Ladybirds will have crowns. I'm sorting it, and I won't let a ceiling collapse take away our end-of-year concert. If anyone wants to help with costumes or with lending me a laminator for a week, please message me.
- **I'm back at school on Wednesday.** Please don't make a big thing of it in front of the children. Thandi did a very normal week. Thandi is a teacher who is going to teach her class about the end of the year. If your child asks, the simple truth is that our building had a fire, nobody was hurt, and we are getting a new place to live.
- If your child has told you something about the fire that worries you, please message me. I'd rather hear it from you.

## About replying

My phone has been going mad since Saturday. I read everything. I am just answering slowly — some days I'll get to a lot of comments, some days I won't get to any. I won't be ignoring you. If you need me urgently, please reply to a comment on the BackaBuddy page and Zinhle will flag it to me.

## Thank you

I genuinely don't know what to say about how good people have been. Uncle Faizel in his vest and slippers. Zinhle, who set the page up and wouldn't let me argue. My sister. The school families. The mums who have dropped off soup and offered to keep my cats for a month — Marmalade is currently living her best life indoors, thank you. Random people who have forwarded this letter further than I'd like to think about.

I started writing this letter three times and stopped each time because I kept crying. So I'm going to keep it short, say thank you, and get back to rebuilding my life one day at a time.

If you can, please share the BackaBuddy link. If you can't, please share the warning about the fake page. Both help.

With a very grateful, very tired, very okay heart,

**Thandi**
Flat 12, Lindale Court, Station Road, Observatory
(Still a teacher. Still the Ladybirds' teacher. Still got 22 crowns to make.)

---

A few quick notes before you send it:

- The last line of the letter (the "22 crowns to make" bit) is a bit of a joke — if you'd rather it not read that way, cut it and just end on "Still got 22 crowns to make." on its own.
- Where the letter mentions your sister's gate drop-off, I softened it slightly — you may want to name the mum if you're close, or leave it as is. Some people will read "please don't do it like that" as a rebuke; if that's not how you meant it, swap in "it made me feel awkward, but thank you" instead.
- Add your sister's number under "About replying" if you're comfortable, and delete the bracketed instruction at the top so it doesn't get forwarded.
